Present Yourselves
prih-ZENT yor-SELVZ
phrase
From Romans 12:1; the charge to offer the whole self to God as a living sacrifice.

Biblical Definition

Present yourselves is the apostle Paul’s charge at the turning-point of Romans, where, having set forth the mercies of God through eleven chapters of doctrine, he turns to exhortation: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. The word present is the language of the altar—to offer, to yield up—but the sacrifice is not a slain beast but the believer’s own self, a living sacrifice, the whole man given over to God for His service. It is grounded wholly in grace: by the mercies of God—the response of gratitude for all that the gospel has freely given, not a price to earn it. Paul presses the same word elsewhere: yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God. To present oneself is to make a deliberate, total, and reasonable surrender of body and soul to the Lord who bought it—reasonable, for it is the only fitting response to such mercy. It is followed at once by the call not to be conformed to this world, but to be transformed by the renewing of the mind. The dictionary honors this charge as the gateway of the consecrated life: that the believer, moved by the mercies of God, yields his whole self a living sacrifice to God—the reasonable, grateful, and total surrender that is the beginning of true holiness.

Webster 1828 Definition

Paul’s charge (Rom 12:1) to offer the whole self to God as a living sacrifice, moved by His mercies; the grateful, total surrender that begins the consecrated life.

PRESENT YOURSELVES, Paul’s charge to offer the self to God (Rom 12:1).

Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God.

The language of the altar: to offer, to yield up.

Grounded in grace: by the mercies of God, not to earn them.

Followed by: be not conformed, but transformed (Rom 12:2).

Key Scripture

Rom 12:1 — "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service."

Rom 6:13 — "Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God."

Rom 12:2 — "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God."

2Co 8:5 — "And this they did, not as we hoped, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God."

Modern Corruption

Consecration is made a means to earn God’s favor, or reduced to partial, occasional surrender; Scripture grounds it in grace and calls for the whole self offered.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Two errors attend the charge to present oneself. The first makes consecration a means to earn God’s favor—a sacrifice offered to buy His acceptance—reversing the gospel order. The second reduces it to a partial, occasional surrender, yielding a corner of life while keeping the rest. But Paul’s charge is grounded in grace and demands the whole: by the mercies of God, present your bodies a living sacrifice (Rom 12:1)—the response of gratitude for mercy already received, and the offering not of a part but of the whole self.

The principle to recover is the grateful, total, reasonable surrender of the self to God. The motive is mercy: only after eleven chapters setting forth the riches of grace does Paul say, I beseech you therefore, by the mercies of God. The offering is the whole man, a living sacrifice; the manner is deliberate and complete, as the Macedonians first gave their own selves to the Lord (2 Cor 8:5); the fruit is transformation, not conformity to the world (Rom 12:2). To present oneself is the gateway of the consecrated life: yielding body and soul to the Lord who bought them, as those that are alive from the dead (Rom 6:13)—the reasonable service that is the beginning of true holiness, flowing not from fear or merit but from grateful love.
